# code3d/lib index (generated by tools/lib_index.py; do not edit by hand)

One line per public top-level function and class, with the first docstring line. Plan reuse from here and `assets/patterns.md`;
read a library only for the functions a plan names. Regenerate after adding or changing a library.

## asc_rig.py: Rig of production 017 (what if an elevator cable is cut): the shaft with rails, landings and a governor wheel in the pit, the car (closed or cut away), its stee
- `ease(k)`
- `fall_z(t, t0, z0, g, floor)` Base height of a car released at t0 from z0, falling under g, stopping at `floor`.
- `fall_v(t, t0, g, z0, floor)`
- class `Mats` Materials by gate role. Hero colours come from scenes.json hero_colours (the module constants are only the fallbacks); the shaft wall and the landings take the
- `lights(S)` The stage lights ride with the subject: the shaft is tall and the lights are fixed. Returns f(dz) to raise them.
- `look(S, target, radius, el, az)`
- `shaft(S, H, m)` Back wall, landings with doors, two guide rails, the pit slab, the top beam and the sheave.
- `governor_wheel(m, cab, name)` The car-mounted overspeed governor: a spoked wheel that rolls on the outer face of the right rail, on a bracket from the car side, with two fly-weights on arms.
- `gov_set(g, angle, open_k)`
- class `Cab` The car. `root` carries it (set `root.location.z` each frame); parts are children. open_front cuts the front away to show the inside (scene 4). methods: set_z
- `safety_gear(cab, m, name)` The grip on the rails (rung 2 of the 017 reshape: the clamp hardware failed blind naming in seven readings, so it stays off screen). Per rail one accent sleeve
- `gear_set(cab, k)` k 0 -> 1: the accent sleeves grow along the rails around the car's base (the car is held by its rails).
- class `Ropes` n parallel steel ropes from the car roof to the top beam, each in two parts: the upper one (world) and the stub on the roof (child of the car), so a cut leaves methods: set
- class `Buffer` The pit buffer: sleeve, rod and cap plate. set(s): s = how far the rod has sunk into the sleeve (0..STROKE). methods: top0, set
- `phone(S, m, parent, name)` A chunky phone slab (exaggerated: the car is 26 wide, the phone 7.5): bezel, dark screen, camera dot. Returns the root empty.

## caca_rig.py: Rig of production 016 (how many kilos of poop in a lifetime): the stylised stool unit, its pile (ONE mesh of many units, rewritten per frame), the kitchen scale
- `unit_template(rings, segs, seed)` Unit-length (x, -0.5..0.5) stool: a bent, lumpy, tapered log, one end rounded and fat, the other drawn to a soft tip. Returns (verts (n,3), faces).
- `swirl_template(rings, segs, seed)` A coiled, tapering soft-serve swirl (2.5 turns, tip curling over): the form viewers name as poop. Unit width ~0.7 (x, y), base at z = 0, centred on x, y.
- `stool_material(S, hex_color, name)` Matte, slightly satin; never wet (the gross stays conceptual).
- `rot_matrices(n, rnd, flat)` n random rotations; flat keeps the unit mostly lying down (yaw free, small tilt) so a pile reads as units resting on units.
- class `Pile` n stool units in ONE mesh (variants of the template cycle so a pile has no repeats in a row). set(pos (n,3), size (n,)) rewrites every vertex: size 0 hides a un methods: set
- `mound(n, centre, radius, height, seed, floor)` Resting positions of n units heaped into a cone-ish mound (low units first in index order, so a growing count builds the pile from the bottom up).
- class `Set`
- `bathroom(S, colours)` The library toilet (lid down, seat up) on the stage floor. Returns the parts the scenes animate.
- `bathroom_scale(S, loc)` Kitchen scale: slab body, steel platter, a dark display window. Geometric and reads instantly (route: code primitive). Returns (root, display_empty).

## caca_set.py: Set pieces of production 016 beyond the frozen hero (caca_rig): the lighter pile for big heaps, retinting of the library props (suitcase, horse, cars), the see-
- class `LitePile` Same as Pile with a lighter unit mesh (a heap of hundreds of units): fewer rings and segments, so one mesh stays under ~250k vertices.
- `lerp_mound(n, a, b, k, seed)` Positions of n units on a mound blending layout a -> b by k (each a dict centre/radius/height); the same random draws, so the heap swells in place.
- `flight(i, n, t, t0, t1, src, dst, arc, fly, power)` Unit i of n: released between t0 and t1 (later units later), flies src -> dst in an arc, then rests. Returns (xyz, shown).
- `retint_prop(objs, rules)` rules: list of (name substring or '*', hex, role, rough, coat); first match wins per material.
- `suitcase(S, loc, rot, name_root)`
- `horse(S, loc, rot)`
- `car(S, loc, rot)`
- `tank(S, loc, size, wall)` Glass tank (five thin glass slabs) and a water block whose height is set per frame: returns (water_obj, set_level(frac)).
- `seesaw(S, pivot, length, width, thick)` Plank on a triangular fulcrum. Returns (root, angle_setter(deg)): positive = right end down. Parts of the heap are rotated about the pivot by the caller.
- `widen_floor(k)` The stage floor is a finite shadow-catcher plane: scale it for wide shots so its edge never shows.
- `rot_y(points, ang_deg, pivot)` Rotate (n,3) points about the y axis through pivot; positive angle = +x end goes down.

## cepillo_rig.py: Rig of production 012 (toothbrush beside the toilet): the bathroom set from library assets, the bowl water sheet and the droplet beads. Runs inside Blender. Sce
- `retint(mat, hex_color, role, rough, coat)` Named role + flat colour. The library materials drive Base Color from textures, so the link is cut first (asset_rig.retint only sets the default value).
- `tiled_wall(S, hexc)`
- class `Set`
- `bathroom(S, colours, cup_at)` Toilet (lid open), sink against the wall, cup of toothbrushes on the sink's ledge, toilet brush in its holder, tiled wall. Returns the parts the scenes animate.

- class `Plume` The droplets' life as a deterministic function: rise (u 0..1), hang (drift t), settle (u toward targets). All positions in cm; the same seed gives the same clou methods: rise, hang, settle, landing

## cheap_kit.py: Cheap material routes for expensive element classes (playbook: docs/current/specs/render-cost-playbook.md; measured on production 008's heaviest scene).
- `ice_milky(name, tint, core, seed, clip, strength)` Ice with no volume: the noise gate that drove the volumetric core instead lowers transmission on the surface, so cloudy patches read as milky ice.
- `no_volume(m)` Drop a material's volume entirely (context water with a faint absorption, for instance).
- `thin_wall(m)` One refraction event per surface: a glass shell stops bending what is behind it, and transmission depth falls.
- `fake_indirect(m)` Context glass only: indirect diffuse and glossy rays pass straight through. Camera rays still see glass. Never on an element under test without a re-read.

## clock_rig.py: Hero rig for the clock video (reloj-coral): the motion work of a wall clock as a COMPOUND gear train, built from gear_rig's Gear class.
- `mesh_angle(th_driver, phi, n_driver, n_driven)` Driven gear's mesh angle for a driver angle (tooth meets gap exactly; speed ratio n_driver / n_driven, reversed).

- `thd0()` D's mesh angle at zero input (hour-hand reference, so the hour hand starts at a fixed pose).

## common.py: code3d shared library (runs inside Blender): identity palette, exact colours, render setup, studio world, camera.
- `linear(hex_color, alpha)` sRGB hex -> linear RGBA (Blender works in linear space; exact hex values need this conversion).
- `identity(production)`
- `palette(vi)` name -> hex, plus 'backdrop' (the spec background).
- `parse_args()` Arguments after `--`: key=value pairs (production, mode, frames, out ...).
- `reset_scene()`
- `setup_render(scene, mode)` draft = half resolution + few samples (iteration); final = 1080x1920 + more samples (rendered once).
- `studio_world(scene, backdrop_hex, hdri, strength)` HDRI lights the scene; the camera sees the exact backdrop colour (mix on 'Is Camera Ray').
- `principled(name, hex_color, roughness, metallic, subsurface)`
- `append_material(blend, name)` Link-free append of a library material (never re-download: assets live in code3d/assets).
- `make_camera(scene, lens)`
- `orbit(cam, target, radius, elevation_deg, azimuth_deg)` Place the camera on a sphere around `target`: azimuth 0 = looking along +y from the -y side.
- `add_light(scene, kind, location, energy, size, target)`
- `smooth(a, b, t)`
- `render_frames(scene, out_dir, start, end)`

## composition.py: Frame-composition probe (Blender side). After a beauty still, render a flat "class mask" still of the same frame: every material is replaced
- `begin_masks(scene)` Replace every material by its class emission, the world by flat magenta, and strip bloom/denoise: call ONCE after the beauty stills.
- `save_mask_still(scene, path)`

## gear_rig.py: Hero rig for the gear-ratio video (engranajes-papel): a COMPOUND spur-gear train, hard surfaces only, one rig revisited in every scene.
- `gear_mesh(name, n, material, thick)` Spur gear with trapezoid teeth, extruded along local +z (centred), pitch radius n*M/2.
- class `Gear` One gear: an empty carries world position/plane (rotated so mesh-z = world -y); `spin` (the mesh) rotates about its axle. methods: set_angle, scale_all
- class `Train` Six shafts: pinion_0 (input) ... big_5 (output). Pair k = pinion on shaft k meshing big on shaft k+1, direction PHI[k] in the XZ plane. methods: plane, angles, input_for_output, set_input, pop
- `block_and_floor(m, x, z)` Heavy ink block for the force scene.

- `heat_volume(S, name, size, loc, hex_color, density, strength, scale)` A box of emissive, noise-modulated volume: a thermal plume / glow in the same physical language as the rest of the scene. Returns (object, w_input) - animate th

- `noshadow(*objs)` Glass, water and ice must not block shadow rays (Cycles treats refractive surfaces as opaque for light: the contents of a glass go black, measured 2026-11-05 on

- `cone_needle(name, p0, p1, r_tail, r_tip, material)` A chunky straight needle from tail p0 to tip p1 (a tapered cone, rounded tail).

- `bar_between(name, p0, p1, radius, material)` A chunky rounded bar from p0 to p1 (cartoon limbs, tweezer arms, pincers).

## soap_rig.py: Rig for 009 (jabon-agua-sola-no-quita-grasa): palette, a soap molecule (head + tail, ONE joined mesh, head along +z), orientation and sphere-point helpers.
- `palette(S)`
- `molecule(S, M, name)` Head sphere at +z, tail cylinder below; one mesh with two materials (cloneable by swarm).
- `face(direction)` Euler that turns local +z (the head) toward `direction`.
- `sphere_points(n, seed)` Fibonacci sphere: n unit vectors spread evenly.
- `ease(a, b, t)`

## stage.py: Shared stage for code3d scenes (runs inside Blender): materials, studio world, camera, key light, and the runner that
- class `Stage`  methods: run

## suture.py: Reusable code3d objects for the suturing scenes (runs inside Blender): skin halves, wound floor, curved needle, thread.
- `box(name, x0, x1, y0, y1, z0, z1, material, bevel, parent)`
- `skin_half(side, gap_half, width, length, skin_mat, tissue_mat)` One side of the cut (side = -1 left, +1 right): an empty carrying a skin layer over a tissue block.
- `wound_floor(gap_half, length, floor_z, tissue_mat)`
- `curved_needle(radius, center_z, tip_deg, arc_deg, r_tail, r_tip, material)` A tapered tube along an arc of the circle (centre (0, 0, center_z), x-z plane). Its origin is the circle
- `arc_points(cx, cz, radius, a0_deg, a1_deg, step_deg, y)`
- `resample(poly, n)` Evenly spaced n points along a polyline (so the thread keeps a constant point count while it changes).
- class `Thread` A thin tube whose polyline is rewritten every frame (frame handler), at a constant point count. methods: set
- `knot_polyline(form, tight, center, reach, base_z, scale_loose, scale_tight, m)` A thread along x through `center` that ties an overhand (trefoil) knot.

## tape_rig.py: huincha-de-medir: the hero TAPE-MEASURE rig on the dark stage (runs inside Blender; EEVEE drafts, Cycles finals).
- `ease_out(p)`
- `back(k, s_)`
- `show(obj, visible)` Hide by parking far below the stage (toggling hide_render per frame crashed Blender 5.2 with Freestyle; kept for safety).
- `pbr(name, folder, prefix, base_hex, metallic, rough_mul, scale, normal, tint_mix, coat)` A PBR material from an ambientCG folder (Color / Roughness / NormalGL), colour-keyed to the palette hex: the texture supplies
- `plain(name, hex_color, rough, metallic, coat)`
- `gold_emit(name, hex_color, strength)`
- `ticks_image()` The unnumbered tick tile: fine ticks every 0.1 BU, mid every 0.5, long every 1.0 (BU), ~410 px per BU; red channel = ink mask.
- `blade_material(pal, hex_steel, metallic)` Brushed steel (ambientCG Metal012, box-mapped) with the printed ticks (UV) and a GOLD stress glow driven by three node values
- `materials(pal)`
- class `Stage`  methods: run
- `begin(default_slot, floor_z)`
- `look(stage, target, radius, el, az)`
- `rbox(name, size, loc, material, bevel, seg, parent, rot)` A bevelled box of full size (x, y, z).
- `cyl(name, radius, length, loc, material, axis, parent, verts, bevel)`
- `empty(name, loc, parent)`
- class `Blade` The blade as one mesh whose vertices are rewritten every frame. Centreline from a tangent-angle profile theta(s) (rotation about y, methods: set, z_at, x_at, set_fast, stress
- `spiral_strip(name, r_in, r_out, turns, width, material, steps, thick, twist, loc)` A flat strip wound in a spiral in the x-z plane (axis along y): r = r_in + (r_out - r_in) * a / (2 pi turns). Returns (obj, rebuild)
- class `Tape` The whole hero rig. `root` hangs the housing; the blade is NOT parented (placed in world coordinates by `place_blade`). The housing is methods: set_coil, mouth, S, place_blade

## thermos_real.py: Real thermos for 009 (every-element remake 2026-11-05). Runs inside Blender (Cycles, `transparent` profile).
- `add_cut(mat, z0, z1)` Make `mat` transparent in a front window: where world y < the 'cut' Value and z0 < z < z1. Returns the Value node (set outputs[0].default_value per frame).
- `hot_steel(name, hex_color)` Polished steel whose emission can be raised (the wall warming up): returns (material, emission strength input).
- `thermos(S, loc, enamel)` Build the cut-away thermos. Returns a dict: cuts (list of Value nodes to animate together), hot (emission input of the inner wall), parts.
- `set_cut(P, y)`
- `cap(S, mat, loc)` The stopper-cup of a vacuum flask (redesigned 2026-11-07, after blind readers called the ribbed grey disc with a knob a battery / flashlight): a steel CUP, flar
- `front_light(strength)` A big emissive panel in front of the camera side, invisible to the camera: lights the inside of the cut-away (reflections and refraction), like a softbox.
- `steam_column(S, name, size, loc, density, scale)` Soft steam: a box whose DENSITY (not only emission) is noise-masked, tapered radially and faded at both ends, so no box edge shows. Returns (object, w_input).

## titanic_rig.py: Rig of production 026 (why the Titanic sank if they said it was unsinkable): a stylised ocean liner built from primitives (no livery, no name), with a closed ex
- `lerp(a, b, k)`
- `hw(x)` Outer half-beam at x: a pointed bow, a blunt stern.
- `hd(x)` Outer depth below the deck at x.
- `sec(x, a, inset)` A point of the hull section at x, angle a (0 = the near deck edge, pi/2 = the keel line, pi = the far deck edge).
- `profile(x, level, n, inset)` The far half of the section at x, from the keel line up the far wall to `level`, closed back along the surface: [(y, z)], n + 2 points.
- `mesh_obj(name, mat, parent)`
- `loft(o, rows, close, thick)` rows: list of rings of (x, y, z); a surface between consecutive rings.
- class `Mats` Hero colours come from scenes.json hero_colours (module constants are the fallbacks); the plate and board take the production's support colours.
- class `Liner` One liner. root carries the pitch and the sink; lid (deck, deckhouse, boats) and near (the near half of the hull) lift away for the cutaway. methods: add_slits, glow, update, slit_state
- class `Sea` The open sea: a wide translucent slab whose top is the waterline (exterior scenes), or the front panels that stand for the sea beside a cutaway hull. methods: hide
- class `Panels` Thin sea panels in front of the cut plane, with a hole where the hull is, so the hull interior stays dry and the waterline reads across the picture; `fill` clos methods: fill, show
- class `Iceberg` A faceted, lumpy iceberg: a big mass below the waterline, a ragged peak above. root is placed by the scene (z = the waterline).

## toilet_rig.py: Hero rig for the toilet video (inodoro-donde-va-todo): a CUTAWAY toilet, side profile in the XZ plane (camera looks along +y, the bowl faces +x).
- `material_set()`
- `prism(name, poly, y0, y1, material, smooth)`
- `rect(x0, x1, z0, z1)`
- `carve(obj, cutters)` Boolean-difference every cutter out of obj (exact solver), apply, delete the cutters.
- `cavities(y0, y1)`
- `bevel(o, width)`
- class `Box` A unit cube positioned/scaled each frame: used for the rectangular water pieces. methods: set
- class `PolyWater` A convex polygon prism clipped by z <= level (analytic Sutherland-Hodgman on the horizontal plane): the bowl water. methods: set
- class `Toilet`  methods: state, flap, press, put_waste, path_point
- `cpu_draft(stage, args)` Development previews that must not touch the GPU while a final render runs: Cycles on 4 CPU threads, tiny and noisy.
- `keys(t, pts)` Smoothstep-interpolated value of the piecewise key list [(t0, v0), (t1, v1), ...] at time t (holds the ends).
- `ring(m, name, loc, sx, sz, minor)` Accent torus facing the camera (x, z radii): marks a region; hidden by scale.
- `gas_material()`

## toon.py: True cel/toon rendering pass (runs inside Blender), opt-in per production via `"render_style": "toon"` in scenes.json.
- `band_hexes(hex_color)` (lit, shadow, deep): lit = the exact hex; the others keep hue and saturation and scale the HSV value.
- `outline_hex(backdrop_hex)`
- `make_material(name, hex_color)` A new toon material authored directly (for objects modelled in the toon language from the first object).
- `restyle_materials(pal)` Every named material, modelled or downloaded, becomes a toon material of its palette hex.
- `key_light_and_ambient()` One hard-shadow sun in the old key light's direction; the HDRI only fills ambient light (camera sees the backdrop).
- `outlines(scene, backdrop_hex)` Freestyle: same colour, same pixel width on every object; fern cards and the jungle plane are left out.
- `apply(production, scene)`

## voz_rig.py: Rig of production 018 (why your voice sounds strange when recorded): the library skull (human-skull, one mesh, faces -Y) as speaker and as listener, a chunky ph
- `ease(k)`
- `stage_set(S, x0, x1)` Cream cutaway plate behind the cast and the ink plinth under it.
- `skull_material(S, hexc)` Bone: flat Principled in the hero's bone colour, mixed toward the accent emission by the Value node `vib` (0 = plain bone, 1 = lit in the accent).
- class `Skull`  methods: glow, world, mouth, ear, pose
- `load_skull(S, loc, yaw, mat, pop)`
- `clone_skull(S, src, loc, yaw, pop)` A linked copy of the loaded skull with its own bone material (so its glow never lights).
- class `Phone`  methods: set_dot, set_bars
- class `Pool` n accent torus rings (major radius 1, scaled per frame). `put` places one; unused rings stay at EPS. methods: put, off
- `aim(vec)` Euler rotation that points a torus's axis (local z) along vec.
- `air(pool, t, emits, origin, target, speed, r0, grow, stop)` Rings leave `origin` at each time in `emits`, travel toward `target` at `speed`, widen with distance and are absorbed at `stop` (default: the target). Returns t
- `profile(z_m)` Rough horizontal extent of the skull (fraction of its widest) at asset height z (metres): the dome narrows toward the crown, the jaw toward the chin.
- `climb(pool, t, emits, dur, z0, z1)` Bone rings: horizontal ellipses hugging the skull (children of its root) that climb from the jaw to the crown.
- `ear_pulse(pool, t, emits, side, dur, r0, r1)` Rings that spread on the skull's side at the ear canal (children of its root, axis along local x).
- `zigzag(S, a, b, n, amp, r, grow)` A jagged red line from a to b: the voice as the phone is feared to hand it back.
- `unspool(zig, k)` Retract a zigzag from its start (k 0 -> 1): the belief dissolving.

## wrinkle_rig.py: Rig for 006 (pieles-arrugadas-agua): palette, a stylised fingertip (rounded solid, optional ridge rings), a water tank, a nerve line with signal pulses.
- `palette(S)`

- `tank(S, M, x, w, d, h, z0, **tk)` Translucent water block standing on the floor; returns the box (surface at z0+h).
